title: Read: hiragana extras
description: Voiced sounds, combined sounds and more. Learn the basic characters first.

units.title: G sounds
intro: Two small marks, called dakuten, turn a sound into its voiced partner. Put them on the K row and you get the G row: ga, gi, gu, ge, go.
The character keeps its shape. Only the two marks are new: か becomes が, き becomes ぎ.
The g is always hard, as in 'go', never soft as in 'giraffe'.

items.hint: Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'ga'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'gi'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'gu'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'ge'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'go'.

units.title: Z sounds
intro: The same two marks on the S row give the Z row: za, ji, zu, ze, zo.
Two surprises: し becomes じ (ji, as in 'jeep') and す becomes ず (zu).
ぢ and づ sound exactly like じ and ず. They are rare, so we skip them and write じ and ず.

items.hint: Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'za'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'ji'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'zu'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'ze'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'zo'.

units.title: D sounds
intro: The T row with dakuten gives the D row. Only three are common: da, de, do.
ち and つ also have voiced forms (ぢ and づ), but they sound like じ and ず and appear in only a few words, so we skip them.

items.hint: Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'da'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'de'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'do'.

units.title: B sounds
intro: The H row with dakuten gives the B row: ba, bi, bu, be, bo.
The two marks sit at the top right, the same as on every other voiced character.

items.hint: Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'ba'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'bi'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'bu'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'be'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'bo'.

units.title: P sounds
intro: The H row can also take a small circle, called handakuten. That gives the P row: pa, pi, pu, pe, po.
Two marks means B. A circle means P. Check which one before you read.

items.hint: Same shape as the plain character, with a small circle at the top right: 'pa'.
Same shape as the plain character, with a small circle at the top right: 'pi'.
Same shape as the plain character, with a small circle at the top right: 'pu'.
Same shape as the plain character, with a small circle at the top right: 'pe'.
Same shape as the plain character, with a small circle at the top right: 'po'.

units.title: Combined sounds: きゃ, ぎゃ
intro: A small や, ゆ or よ after a character in the 'i' column blends the two into one sound. き and ゃ make きゃ (kya).
The small character is about half the size and sits low and to the right. It does not get its own beat: kya is one sound, not ki-ya.
Compare きや (ki-ya, two beats) with きゃ (kya, one beat).

items.hint: き plus a small ゃ: say 'kya' as one sound, one beat.
き plus a small ゅ: say 'kyu' as one sound, one beat.
き plus a small ょ: say 'kyo' as one sound, one beat.
ぎ plus a small ゃ: say 'gya' as one sound, one beat.
ぎ plus a small ゅ: say 'gyu' as one sound, one beat.
ぎ plus a small ょ: say 'gyo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Combined sounds: しゃ, じゃ
intro: With し and じ the i drops away completely: しゃ is sha, not shi-ya. じゃ is ja.
So the pattern is sha, shu, sho and ja, ju, jo.

items.hint: し plus a small ゃ: say 'sha' as one sound, one beat.
し plus a small ゅ: say 'shu' as one sound, one beat.
し plus a small ょ: say 'sho' as one sound, one beat.
じ plus a small ゃ: say 'ja' as one sound, one beat.
じ plus a small ゅ: say 'ju' as one sound, one beat.
じ plus a small ょ: say 'jo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Combined sounds: ちゃ, にゃ
intro: ち and に also combine: ちゃ is cha, にゃ is nya.
Same rule: the small や, ゆ or よ is half size and joins the sound before it.

items.hint: ち plus a small ゃ: say 'cha' as one sound, one beat.
ち plus a small ゅ: say 'chu' as one sound, one beat.
ち plus a small ょ: say 'cho' as one sound, one beat.
に plus a small ゃ: say 'nya' as one sound, one beat.
に plus a small ゅ: say 'nyu' as one sound, one beat.
に plus a small ょ: say 'nyo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Combined sounds: ひゃ, みゃ
intro: ひ and み combine the same way: ひゃ is hya, みゃ is mya.
These are less common than the earlier ones, but they turn up in numbers like 100.

items.hint: ひ plus a small ゃ: say 'hya' as one sound, one beat.
ひ plus a small ゅ: say 'hyu' as one sound, one beat.
ひ plus a small ょ: say 'hyo' as one sound, one beat.
み plus a small ゃ: say 'mya' as one sound, one beat.
み plus a small ゅ: say 'myu' as one sound, one beat.
み plus a small ょ: say 'myo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Combined sounds: りゃ, びゃ
intro: り and び also combine: りゃ is rya, びゃ is bya.
Remember that Japanese r is a quick tongue tap.

items.hint: り plus a small ゃ: say 'rya' as one sound, one beat.
り plus a small ゅ: say 'ryu' as one sound, one beat.
り plus a small ょ: say 'ryo' as one sound, one beat.
び plus a small ゃ: say 'bya' as one sound, one beat.
び plus a small ゅ: say 'byu' as one sound, one beat.
び plus a small ょ: say 'byo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Combined sounds: ぴゃ
intro: The last combined sounds: ぴゃ, ぴゅ, ぴょ (pya, pyu, pyo).
These are rare. You will see them mostly in sound words like ぴょんぴょん (boing, boing).

items.hint: ぴ plus a small ゃ: say 'pya' as one sound, one beat.
ぴ plus a small ゅ: say 'pyu' as one sound, one beat.
ぴ plus a small ょ: say 'pyo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Small っ and long vowels
intro: A small っ means: pause briefly, then say the next consonant twice. きて is 'kite', but きって is 'kit-te', with a held beat in the middle.
You do not pronounce っ by itself. It is silence, one beat long. It is half the size of つ and sits low on the line.
Long vowels are written by adding another vowel kana: あ after あ-column sounds, い after い or え sounds, う after う or お sounds. おかあさん (mother) has two beats on 'aa'. とうきょう (Tokyo) is 'toh-kyoh'.
Hold a long vowel for about two beats. Short and long vowels change the word: おばさん (aunt) vs おばあさん (grandmother).

items.meaning: a short pause: the next consonant is doubled
items.hint: Looks like つ but half the size and low on the line. Say nothing: hold the next consonant a beat longer.
